svg.text: Intelligent Refund Risk & Resolution Platform - end-to-end architecture
Intelligence layer on top of an existing refund process: real-time LangGraph pipeline + offline historical loop + offline evaluation (state after the 2026-10-22 real-data run)
1 REAL-TIME PATH (one claim in, one decision out - seconds)
Calls the API only - no decision logic
the claim is parked for a human.
LangGraph real-time orchestration (graph.py) - "AI recommends; existing systems execute"
Features, formulas, abuse rules, expected cost and guardrails are deterministic. Agents interpret text / image / history, explain, and may only escalate.
• refund window, refundable?, auto-approve limit, order
• violation -> policy_decline; no AI output can relax
• refunds in 30 / 90 / 180 days, refund value ratio
• reuse vs other customers' stored evidence; optional
• claim interpretation: negation-aware rules (default); optional zero-shot transformer
• outputs: ambiguity 0-100, evidence inconsistency 0-100, evidence confidence, flags
• sentiment (VADER default; multilingual XLM-R recommended) -> CX routing only
• optional LLM / CLIP: bounded +/-10 points, never a decision
• Behavioural Risk = .35 frequency + .25 value ratio + .15 repeat reason + .15 return
• Trust Index = 100 - BR (supporting only); blacklist = hard signal, not weighted
• 5 abuse patterns: serial refunder, return abuse, fake defect, refund farming, policy
4 Abuse + Claim Risk Synthesis (decision state, all scores 0-100)
Claim Risk = .30 ambiguity + .30 evidence inconsistency + .20 evidence reuse + .20 abuse-pattern strength | Exposure risk = (0.6 x Claim Risk + 0.4 x Behavioural Risk) /
• cheapest eligible action wins; COST_SCALE default 1.0, 0.1 recommended
• policy violation -> policy_decline (AI can never override)
• exact evidence copy used by another customer -> manual_review
• writes the rationale: lowest expected cost and the margin, or the guardrail that
• may only ESCALATE to a more cautious action (LLM optional)
• persists claim, scores, flags, costs, evidence, features, risk profile
• calls the EXISTING system for the chosen action; audit log; cx_priority flag
Safe failure: any node error -> fallback_manual_review (flag system_error_routed_to_review, review case opened) - never a silent approval or decline
window days, refundable, auto-approve limit per category
flag_cx_priority -> care outreach (changes who contacts the
2 SQL DATA STORE (db.py) - SQLite for the MVP, PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL
• separate DB - the demo DB is never
3 HISTORICAL INTELLIGENCE & PREVENTION LOOP (offline - never called inside the real-time graph; a test enforces it)
• e.g. QC audit, listing fix, policy
Flags from the loop reach later claims only as CONTEXT for the agents - they never change a formula or a guardrail. Results are shown in the Management View (Prevention loop tab).
4 OFFLINE EVALUATION, DATA & TOOLING (eval_data.py -> eval_data.db; separate from the live database)
Sources and labels (provenance on every row: source | assumed | synthetic)
1 policy gate vs Olist: agreement 1.0 (9,000 checks) 2 UCI behaviour flag rates
3 Copydays validation / test split (NOT RUN) 4 abuse scenarios + 4b cost sweep
5 claim NLP + sentiment (+ nlp_error_analysis.json) 6 Olist reviews 7 Amazon
Tooling (all reproducible; raw data stays out of GitHub)
label_tools.py (split, kappa, reconcile, finalize) validate_backends.py (real transformer / CLIP
pytest: 53 passed. Live run: FastAPI 19/19 checks (normal, policy decline, evidence request,
repeat refunder, reused image, human resolve, historical loop) + Streamlit 3 pages render.
Sentiment: XLM-R recall(neg) 0.76 vs VADER 0.22 (developer labels). CLIP: not validated.
